name: Battle of Tagliacozzo
summary: At the Battle of Tagliacozzo (August 23, 1268), Charles of Anjou, with papal and French backing, defeats and kills Conradin, the 16-year-old last Hohenstaufen claimant, ending the dynasty's struggle for the kingdom of Sicily. Charles's general Erard de Valéry feigned retreat to break the Staufen advance, then counterattacked with a reserve force held in concealment. Conradin was captured fleeing, publicly beheaded in Naples, and his supporter Frederick of Austria executed with him. The executions shocked contemporaries; Dante places Charles in Purgatorio for this act.

_quarry.structural_significance: Ends the Hohenstaufen dynasty; secures Angevin control of Sicily and southern Italy; the brutality of Conradin's execution becomes a rallying cry for the Sicilian Vespers (1282); creates the political vacuum in Germany that produces the Great Interregnum
